review_scope: Compared all 23 final viewpoints to the published main frames, including the native crop details. The last release's stronger differences at the watch station and signal room are smaller in this capture. Local illumination, reflection and shadow edges still vary. The dumbwaiter viewpoint is obscured by brick. The separate player-route images cover the physical papers, valise and recorder. Human play and artistic acceptance remain open.

images.observation: The pool from the pendant reaches the table and the coloured floor mark. The wall opening remains visible behind the chair; Vantry stays at the right of the table in both frames.
The circular lamp spot spans painted wall and white tile. The curtain edge, cistern and the grout at the lower edge of the light remain distinct.
The apron, the dark object in the resident’s hand and the table edge read against the floor. The blind slats, ceiling pendant and rear workbench retain their positions.
The pool on the rear wall still frames the blind and shelving. Both chair backs stand clear of the table and the right-hand bench remains in shadow.

Both views retain the upper cupboard lip, two work surfaces, basin and drain. The mottled light above the counter and the wall beside the sink differs in brightness. This view does not isolate the cause.
The circular gauge, black firebox door, overhead pipes and low hearth keep their silhouettes. The dedicated player-height pickup view supplies the evidence for the paper and its reachable surface.
The chair back crosses the lower shelves and the umbrella stands beside the far door in both views. The book spines in the shadowed middle shelf have little contrast.
The tile courses turn the corner behind the vertical vent. The pale tank rim, horizontal paper roll and brown return pipe remain separately visible under the dimmer lower-wall light.
The camera faces nearby dark brick in both captures. The seams and the close occluding wall are visible. This camera cannot establish the condition of the lift behind it.
The open leaf reads slightly redder on the candidate. The four circles on the pale plate, overhead supply and lower connections retain their positions.

A mottled brass rail crosses the dark central shape in both frames, between two pale angled supports. Floor grout remains visible. The low sightline limits the character detail this frame can establish.
The small red figure and pale muzzle remain legible along the shelf against the green wall. The framed portrait at left stays very dark in both frames.

The screw heads, long red underside and diagonal support occupy the same positions above the framed pictures and pale bottles. The thin warm highlight at the right edge persists. The underside is dark enough in both frames to limit inspection of the wood grain.

The open compartments remain in the same rows, with the two projecting envelopes in place. The candidate catches more amber light on the rims of the right-hand doors and less on the upper-left occupied slot. The chute, bench and door outlines align. The small labels are dim in both views.

The cast ribs, left end fitting and right valve wheel line up against the window and curtain. The brass fittings are more distinct in the candidate while the open wall at upper left is slightly darker. The bottom of the radiator is cut off in both frames.

The front handrail crosses the same cage bars and the guard still encloses the drive. The motor, roof door and threshold occupy the same positions. The left plaster and landing are darker in the candidate; the shadow change does not break the visible rail or tread edges.

The roof cap, right-side highlight and guard rings align, as do the tank outlet, frame uprights and pale footings. Dark diagonal bracing remains faint in both views. The roof and skyline silhouettes show no visible displacement.

The green front lamp, two orange inserts and glass-frame corners align with main. The left floorboards are more visible in the candidate (mean encoded luma 68 versus 56 in the lower-left floor patch). The top frame catches a warmer reflection and a mottled patch appears on plaster left of the clock. The clock, bookshelf and terminal keep their outlines. The broad concentric bands seen above the bookcase in release01 are not apparent here.

The cream roll and its two black wall brackets line up with the tile courses in both frames. In the candidate, the shadow along the top right edge of the roll has a visible sawtooth contour and the back corner is darker. The mounting geometry retains the same outline.

The multicoloured puddle keeps the same lobed perimeter on the floorboards. The red loops and dark spots remain separately visible against it, clear of the radiator feet and valve. The companion’s display changes slightly at right. This still only shows one instant of the flow.

The reddish strands rise across the same radiator ribs and join the floor puddle at the same position. Highlights pick out the outside strands while the overlapping strands near the centre remain hard to separate in both views. The valve and its clearance remain visible.

The crumb tray is still extended and the loose crumbs, handle, spout and canisters keep their outlines. The candidate has a darker, smoother wall shadow to the left of the kettle and stronger dark reflections on the canisters. The front slots on the toaster have little contrast.

The amber wash on the left wall is visible again. In the same upper-left wall sample, mean encoded luma is 92/255 on published main, 23 on release01 and 111 on this candidate. The gear teeth, brass handle and handrail now catch highlights. The housing and plate keep their positions, and the STATION 1 lettering remains dim.
